summary.root_cause_text: Deploy v1.4 (ledger sync currency handling refactor) corrupted ledger amounts, overstating them versus order amounts.
recommended: Fix the currency handling in the v1.4 sync refactor and add a test that compares ledger amounts to order amounts before redeploying
Confirm the 292 repaired rows with finance, since the count differs from the 12 in the alert

Rolled back version v1.4 -> v1.3. Confirmed: the service is now using the new value.
All business invariants green (health, payments, queue, worker, ledger, errors, latency).

root_causes: Deploy v1.4 (ledger sync currency handling refactor) corrupted ledger amounts, overstating them versus order amounts.
evidence: recent_changes: v1.4 'ledger sync job: currency handling refactor' deployed 2 min before the alert
sync logs show version v1.4 syncing
Payments and queue were healthy (27/27 paid, 0 dropped)
args.impact: 12 ledger entries were mismatched at alert time, with a ledger overstatement of SAR 297055.44 (money_impact). The repair tool reported fixing 292 rows, SAR 7174957.68 recovered. That is more than the 12 flagged, probably because the bad sync kept corrupting rows before the rollback. Orders and payments were unaffected.
recommended_actions: Fix the currency handling in the v1.4 sync refactor and add a test that compares ledger amounts to order amounts before redeploying
Confirm the 292 repaired rows with finance, since the count differs from the 12 in the alert
args.summary: The v1.4 ledger sync refactor wrote wrong amounts to the ledger. I rolled back to v1.3 and repaired the flagged ledger rows. All invariants are green now.
